title: SignalK server
description: Which SignalK server to talk to and how to obtain access. The device identity (clientId) and the token itself live in device state, not here.

keys.name: discovery
keys.title: Discover servers via mDNS
keys.description: Browse _signalk-http._tcp on the local network. Off = only the manual server below. Setting a manual host also stops discovery: an explicit address means that address, so nothing keeps browsing.

keys.name: server_self
keys.title: Preferred server (self URN)
keys.description: Vessel self URN of the discovered server to use, e.g. urn:mrn:signalk:uuid:… Empty = first discovered server with a master role.

keys.name: server_pin
keys.title: Stay on the chosen server
keys.description: Never re-elect a different server once one is in use. The device keeps waiting for it to come back instead of moving to another discovered server. Off = pick a new server if the current one stops answering.

keys.name: server_host
keys.title: Manual server host
keys.description: Host name or IP when mDNS is blocked. Empty = use discovery. When set, this address is used exclusively and mDNS discovery stops.

keys.name: scheme
keys.title: Connection scheme
keys.description: auto = work it out per server: a discovered one by which mDNS service it advertises (_signalk-https._tcp means TLS), a manual host by one unauthenticated probe of http://host:port/signalk that follows a redirect to https. http and https force it. Needs a firmware built with ESPOS_SK_TLS for anything but http; without it the device logs that once and talks http.

keys.name: tls_trust
keys.title: How to trust the server certificate
keys.description: tofu = trust on first use: the first connection pins what the server presents (its CA and the names on the certificate, or the certificate itself when there is no CA) and every later one must match, the way ssh does. ca = hold the server to the CA in ca_pem below instead, for a fleet where the certificates are issued centrally. bundle = the public Mozilla roots only, which refuses the self-signed certificate a boat server normally has. There is no accept-anything mode. Reset a pinned certificate with DELETE /api/v1/sk/tls or the button on the SignalK page.

keys.name: ca_pem
keys.title: CA certificate (PEM)
keys.description: The issuing CA for tls_trust = ca, as a PEM certificate (base64-encoded over the REST API, like any blob). Setting it anchors the device on that CA immediately, so a pre-seeded fleet connects on the first try with nothing to capture. Empty = none; then ca behaves like tofu until one arrives.

keys.name: description
keys.title: Access request description
keys.description: Shown to the admin approving the request. Empty = espOS <hostname>.

keys.name: permissions
keys.title: Requested permissions
keys.description: readwrite is needed to publish deltas.

keys.name: check_s
keys.title: Token check interval
keys.description: How often an approved token is verified against the server (detects revocation).

keys.name: ws_enabled
keys.title: Stream deltas
keys.description: Keep a WebSocket to the server open and send published values as deltas.

keys.name: batch_ms
keys.title: Delta batching window
keys.description: Values published within this window go out as one delta message.

keys.name: timestamps
keys.title: Timestamp deltas
keys.description: Put the time a value was MEASURED on every delta, once the device knows what time it is (see the Clock settings). Without it the server stamps each message when it arrives, so an outage's worth of buffered data lands as one burst at reconnect instead of spread over the hours it was recorded. Off = the old behaviour, and the only reason to want it is a server you would rather have stamp everything itself.

keys.name: buffer_msgs
keys.title: Offline buffer (messages)
keys.description: Delta messages kept while the server is unreachable; oldest are dropped first.

keys.name: drain_per_s
keys.title: Backlog drain rate
keys.description: Buffered messages per second sent after a reconnect, so the server is not swamped.

keys.name: health_s
keys.title: Device health interval
keys.description: Publish uptime, heap, RSSI, reconnects and reset reason this often. 0 = off.

keys.name: stall_s
keys.title: Stream stall before restart
keys.description: WiFi reports connected and the stream has worked since boot, yet it has been down this long: the device raises skLinkStalled as a fatal health condition and the health watchdog restarts it, because a wedged radio link is the one network fault a restart fixes. Generous on purpose so a server restart never reboots the device; raise it if your server takes longer to come back.
